newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia issues 20-year floating rate bond in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Colombia issues 20-year floating rate bond in U.S..

text.p: Colombia quietly raised $120 million in fresh financing through a 20-year floating rate bond placed among a select group of U.S. investors last week in New York, a senior Finance Ministry official said Monday.

Clemente del Valle, the ministry's chief of public credit, said interest on the bond, which is redeemable in eight years if investors choose to cash it in advance of full maturity, had been set at 200 basis points above the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury Bond.
Del Valle said the bond raised Colombia's total sovereign debt issues so far this year to $1.2 billion.

The government was initially authorized to issue $1.1 billion in sovereign debt in 1996, but the central bank agreed to raise the ceiling to $1.4 billion after talks with finance ministry officials in late July.
Del Valle said an additional $180 million would soon be issued in the form of a floating rate mark-denominated bond in Germany. He did not give a specific date for the issue.
The government put plans to launch the bond on hold late last month because of what Del Valle described as minor bureaucratic problems.

Del Valle, who spoke to Reuters in a brief telephone interview, said the government planned to issue $1.8 billion in sovereign debt next year. He conceded, however, that the figure had not yet been approved by the central bank.
